statements.says: The court decides all cases (civil, commercial, maritime, social, real property, family) that fall within its territorial jurisdiction.
Cases are listed before the sections according to the nature of the dispute.
In courts where sections have not been created, the civil section hears all disputes except social cases.
A case listed before the wrong section is sent to the right section through the registry after prior notice to the court president.
General rule: the court of the defendant's domicile; failing a known domicile, the court of his last domicile; with an elected domicile, the court of that domicile; unless the law provides otherwise.
With several defendants, jurisdiction lies with the court of the domicile of any one of them.
Mixed actions go to the court where the property is located.
Compensation for a felony, misdemeanour, minor offence or tort, and actions for damage caused by the administration, go to the court where the harmful act occurred.
Disputes on supplies, works and hire of technical or industrial services go to the court of the place where the agreement was made or performed, even if a party does not reside there.
In commercial matters other than bankruptcy and judicial settlement: the court of the promise or delivery of goods, or of the place of payment; against a company, the court of one of its branches.
Disputes on mail, registered items, declared-value items and postal parcels go to the court of the sender's or the addressee's domicile.
In addition to articles 37, 38 and 46, the listed matters are brought before the listed courts and no others.
Real property matters, works on real property, leases of real property (commercial leases included) and public works go to the court where the property is, or where the works are carried out.

Inheritance, divorce or return, custody, maintenance and housing go respectively to the court of the deceased's domicile, the marital home, the place of custody, the maintenance creditor's domicile, and the place of the housing.
Bankruptcy or judicial settlement of companies and partners' disputes go to the court where the bankruptcy or settlement was opened or where the company has its registered office.
Intellectual property goes to the court sitting at the seat of the judicial council whose area includes the defendant's domicile.
Medical services disputes go to the court in whose area the treatment was given.
Costs of proceedings and fees of judicial assistants go to the court that decided the main case; warranty actions go to the court seized of the main claim.
Seizure matters go to the court in whose area the seizure took place.
Employer-employee disputes go to the court where the employment contract was made or performed, or where the defendant is domiciled.
Exception: where the contract was ended or suspended because of a work accident or occupational illness, the court of the plaintiff's domicile has jurisdiction.
Urgent matters go to the court where the execution difficulty arose or where the measures are sought.
Any clause giving territorial jurisdiction to an incompetent court is void, except between merchants.
Parties may appear voluntarily before a judge even if he lacks territorial jurisdiction.
The parties sign a declaration requesting adjudication; if signing is impossible this is noted.
The judge is competent for the whole proceedings and jurisdiction extends on appeal to the judicial council to which he is attached.
The plea of lack of territorial jurisdiction must be raised before any defence on the merits or plea of inadmissibility.

The family section hears, among others, engagement, marriage, return to the marital home, dissolution and consequences, maintenance, custody, visiting rights, proof of marriage and filiation, kafala, guardianship, interdiction, absence, disappearance and curatorship.
Family section territorial rule: breaking an engagement goes to the court of the defendant's domicile.
Proof of marriage goes to the court of the defendant's domicile.
Divorce or return goes to the court of the marital home; divorce by mutual consent goes to the residence of either spouse as they choose.
Custody, visiting rights and administrative permits for the child in custody go to the place where custody is exercised.
Maintenance goes to the court of the maintenance creditor's domicile.
Household goods go to the court of the marital home.
Authorisation to marry goes to the court of the applicant's place.
Dowry disputes go to the court of the defendant's domicile.
Guardianship goes to the place where guardianship is exercised.
Reconciliation attempts in divorce are mandatory.
Reconciliation attempts must not exceed three months from the filing of the divorce claim.

The social section has exclusive jurisdiction over proof, performance, suspension and termination of work, training and apprenticeship contracts, staff delegate elections, union rights, strikes, social security and retirement, and collective agreements.
Social disputes: territorial jurisdiction lies with the court where the employment contract was made or performed or where the defendant is domiciled.
Exception: after termination or suspension because of a work accident or occupational illness, the court of the plaintiff's domicile.

openPoints.question: Is territorial jurisdiction of public order?
readings: Article 45 voids jurisdiction clauses (except between merchants) and article 40 says 'and no others', which suggests a mandatory rule in those matters.
Articles 46 and 47 let parties appear voluntarily and require the plea before any defence, which suggests the rule can be waived; no text given says the court raises it of its own motion.

openPoints.question: Does article 40 'and no others' exclude voluntary appearance under article 46 and the general rules of 37, 38 and 46?
readings: The text itself names articles 37, 38 and 46 as additional to article 40, so voluntary appearance remains possible.
The words 'and no others' make the article 40 courts the only ones for those matters, so only article 46 is an exception.

openPoints.question: What does 'mixed actions' (39 point 1) mean, and does it conflict with article 40 point 1 for real property?
readings: Mixed actions combine a personal and a real claim, and the court of the property hears them.
Article 40 point 1 covers real property matters and takes precedence for those; the texts given do not define mixed actions.

openPoints.question: Which court applies when both article 39 and article 40 fit (for example a commercial lease claim)?
readings: Article 40 prevails because it is exclusive ('and no others').
Article 39 point 4 may also apply to commercial matters; the texts do not settle the order.

openPoints.question: Is the divorce reconciliation attempt a condition of admissibility or a step within the proceedings?
readings: It is a mandatory step after filing, carried out at the hearing (439, 443 paragraph 4).
It is a prerequisite whose absence could be a defect; no sanction is stated.

openPoints.question: Which court hears divorce when 426 point 3 and 40 point 2 are both considered (marital home)?
readings: Both name the marital home so they agree; 426 adds the mutual-consent case with the residence of either spouse.
